questions.question: Which famous king is this?
questions.explanation: Henry VIII married six times, and he also built up the navy, including the warship Mary Rose.

media.alt: A painting of a broad-shouldered man in rich clothes and a flat cap

questions.question: Which queen is this?
questions.explanation: Victoria became queen at just 18 and reigned for 63 years.

media.alt: An old photograph of an older woman wearing a small crown and veil

questions.question: Who won the Battle of Hastings in 1066 and became King of England?
questions.explanation: William was Duke of Normandy, and the Bayeux Tapestry tells the story of his invasion.

questions.question: Which queen reigned for 70 years, from 1952 to 2022?
questions.explanation: Her reign of 70 years and 214 days is the longest of any British king or queen.

questions.question: In which London building are the Crown Jewels kept?
questions.explanation: They are guarded by the Yeoman Warders, better known as Beefeaters.

questions.question: Which famous French ruler is this?
questions.explanation: Napoleon crowned himself Emperor of the French in 1804.

media.alt: A painting of a man in uniform standing with his hand tucked into his jacket

questions.question: Which English king was nicknamed the Lionheart?
questions.explanation: Richard spent only about six months of his ten-year reign actually in England.

questions.question: In which church has almost every English and British coronation taken place since 1066?
questions.explanation: The abbey's Coronation Chair has been used at coronations for more than 700 years.

questions.question: Cleopatra was the last ruler of which ancient kingdom?
questions.explanation: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.

questions.question: Which queen was on the throne when the Spanish Armada sailed against England in 1588?
questions.explanation: English fireships and fierce storms broke up the Armada, and many of its ships never made it home.

questions.question: In a famous story, which king let some cakes burn while hiding from the Vikings?
questions.explanation: Nobody knows if the story is true, but Alfred did go on to beat the Vikings at the Battle of Edington in 878.

questions.question: In a famous story, which Scottish king was inspired to keep trying by watching a spider spin its web?
questions.explanation: He went on to win a great victory over the English at the Battle of Bannockburn in 1314.

questions.question: Which king agreed to Magna Carta in 1215?
questions.explanation: John did not sign it: he set his royal seal on it at Runnymede, beside the River Thames.

questions.question: Which royal family did Elizabeth I belong to?
questions.explanation: She was the last Tudor monarch, and after her the crown passed to James VI of Scotland.

questions.question: Which royal castle is often called the largest lived-in castle in the world?
questions.explanation: Kings and queens have lived at Windsor for more than 900 years.

questions.question: Which monarch is this?
questions.explanation: She never married and was called the Virgin Queen, which is how the American state of Virginia got its name.

media.alt: A painting of a pale woman with red hair in a jewelled gown and ruff

questions.question: Which French king is this?
questions.explanation: This is Louis XIV, the Sun King, who reigned for 72 years, even longer than Elizabeth II.

media.alt: A painting of a king in a long curly wig and robes

questions.question: Whose remains were found under a car park in Leicester in 2012?
questions.explanation: He was the last English king to die in battle, at Bosworth in 1485.

questions.question: Who was the first Tudor king?
questions.explanation: He married Elizabeth of York, joining the red rose of Lancaster with the white rose of York in the Tudor rose.

questions.question: Which king led the English army at the Battle of Agincourt in 1415?
questions.explanation: Shakespeare gives him the famous band of brothers speech just before the battle.

questions.question: Which king is this?
questions.explanation: Charles I was the only English king to be put on trial and executed, in 1649.

media.alt: A painting of a man with long hair and a pointed beard

questions.question: Who is known as the Nine Days' Queen?
questions.explanation: She was proclaimed queen in July 1553 but was soon pushed aside by Mary I.

questions.question: Which king changed the royal family's name to Windsor in 1917?
questions.explanation: He dropped the German-sounding Saxe-Coburg and Gotha in the middle of the First World War.

questions.question: Which Russian tsar founded the city of St Petersburg in 1703?
questions.explanation: As a young tsar he travelled to Holland and worked in a shipyard under a false name to learn shipbuilding.

questions.question: Which king brought the crowns of England and Scotland together in 1603?
questions.explanation: He had already been James VI of Scotland for almost 36 years when he became James I of England.

questions.question: Which Mughal emperor built the Taj Mahal?
questions.explanation: He built it as a tomb for his beloved wife, Mumtaz Mahal.

questions.question: Who was the last monarch of the House of Stuart?
questions.explanation: None of Anne's children outlived her, so under the Act of Settlement the crown passed to her Protestant German cousin, George of Hanover.

questions.question: Buckingham Palace became the monarch's official London home at the start of whose reign?
questions.explanation: George III bought it in 1761 as a family home, but it only became the monarch's official London residence when Victoria moved in, in 1837.

questions.question: What is the block of sandstone placed in the Coronation Chair when a monarch is crowned?
questions.explanation: Students took it from Westminster Abbey on Christmas Day 1950, and since 1996 it has been kept in Scotland, coming south only for coronations.

questions.question: Which English king was nicknamed Longshanks and the Hammer of the Scots?
questions.explanation: When his tomb was opened in 1774, his body measured about 6 feet 2 inches, very tall for his day.
